note: Literature strongly supports haploinsufficiency across loss-of-function and missense variants with no apparent genotype-phenotype divergence.

evidence.text: De novo variants comprise gene-disrupting and missense variants across FBXO11, with structural modeling in domains such as Zinc-finger UBR suggesting destabilization, and the observed spectrum lacking apparent genotype-phenotype correlations, compatible with haploinsufficiency.

source.title: De novo variants in the F-box protein FBXO11 in 20 individuals with a variable neurodevelopmental disorder
source.quote: This, in combination with the observed spectrum and localization of identified variants and the lack of apparent genotype-phenotype correlations, is compatible with loss of function or haploinsufficiency as an underlying mechanism.

evidence.text: Missense variants across domains including the F-box and Zn-finger UBR domains lead to mislocalization or reduced expression, highlighting haploinsufficiency as the disease mechanism without established genotype-phenotype correlations.

source.title: De novo missense variants in FBXO11 alter its protein expression and subcellular localization
source.quote: Together with the mutational data, our functional results suggest that most missense variants likely lead to a loss of the original FBXO11 function and thereby highlight haploinsufficiency as the most likely disease mechanism for FBXO11-associated NDDs.
